interpretationNote: With 12 types and 18 room placements, each NPC gets 2 base-assigned types plus 1 shared imported type. One of the two base types is also exported into another room, so there are two globally repeated types in each NPC room. 'Two strictly exclusive types + one shared' is mathematically impossible with only 12 types.

weaponInstanceRules.instanceId: Distinct physical copy in an NPC room, required to track traces and access
weaponInstanceRules.copyPolicy: Same weaponId in two rooms denotes distinct physical objects of the same type. Never treat one physical object as simultaneously present in two rooms.
weaponInstanceRules.crimeScenePolicy: Only non-weapon evidence such as marks, residue, records and traces in CRIME_SCENE/LOBBY; no physical weapon instance appears outside 6 NPC personal rooms during investigation.
weaponInstanceRules.timelinePolicy: If a weapon copy was used at the crime scene, a valid case timeline must account for access, transport and return before investigation; otherwise the case is rejected.
weaponInstanceRules.evidencePolicy: Finding a tool alone does not prove it was used, the method or the culprit. Forensic support + NPC knowledge/access + timeline + unique proof graph required.

methodSelectionPolicy.methodScoringPolicy: Accept any of four parent method categories M01-M04 regardless of which of nine subtypes the case uses. Final answer still requires culpritNpcId+methodId+weaponId. If input explicitly mentions subtype, map it to parent and score only parent; do not require subtype ID, do not reject correct parent due to omitted or different subtype wording unless core category itself is unclear.
